content2.content: To get started with Flutter, you need to install it on your machine. Here’s a step-by-step guide for installation on different platforms:

content4.content: Before installing Flutter, ensure your system meets the following requirements:

content5.content:
Operating System: Windows 10 or later (64-bit).
Disk Space: At least 1.64 GB (more for IDE & tools).

content.title: Download the Flutter SDK
bullets:
Go to the official Flutter website:
 🔗 https://flutter.dev/docs/get-started/install/windows
Extract the ZIP file to a desired location (e.g., C:\src\flutter).

content.title: Add Flutter to PATH
bullets: Open Start Menu → Search for "Edit environment variables" → Open it.
Click "New" and add the path to the flutter in folder (e.g., C:\src\flutter\bin).

content.title: Run Flutter Doctor
bullets: Run: `flutter doctor` to check for any dependencies you need to install.
You’ll see warnings (e.g., Android Studio not installed). We’ll fix these next.

content.title: Install Android Studio (for Android Development)
bullets:
Launch Android Studio → Go to Plugins → Search for "Flutter" → Install it.
		This will also prompt you to install Dart (click Yes)

Configure Android SDK:
Open Android Studio → More Actions → SDK Manager.
Install the latest Android SDK and Android SDK Command-line Tools.

content.title: Set Up an Android Emulator
bullets: Open Android Studio → AVD Manager (Android Virtual Device).
Click "Create Virtual Device" → Select a device (e.g., Pixel 5).
Choose a system image (e.g., Android 13 (API 33) → Download if needed.

content.title: Install Visual Studio Code (Optional but Recommended)
bullets: Open VS Code → Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X) → Search for "Flutter" → Install it.
This will also prompt you to install Dart (click Yes).

content.title: Create Your First Flutter App
bullets: Open VS Code or Android Studio.

Create a new Flutter project:
		`flutter create my_first_app`

Navigate to the project folder:
		`cd my_first_app`
You should see a demo app running on your emulator.

content9.content:
macOS Version: macOS 10.14 (Mojave) or later.
Disk Space: ~2.8 GB (for Flutter + IDE + tools).
Tools Needed:
		Xcode (for iOS development).
		Android Studio (for Android development).
		Visual Studio Code (optional but recommended).
		Homebrew (recommended for easier dependency management).

content.title: Install Xcode
bullets: Open App Store → Search for "Xcode" → Install it.(this may take a while, ~10GB+).
After installation, open Xcode → Preferences → Locations → Command Line Tools → Select the latest version.

content.title: Download Flutter SDK
bullets: Download the macOS stable release (.zip file).
Extract the file to a desired location (e.g., ~/development/flutter):

content.title: Add Flutter to PATH
bullets:
Open your shell config file (depends on your shell):
Bash: ~/.bash_profile or ~/.bashrc
Zsh: ~/.zshrc (default on macOS Catalina+)

Add the Flutter bin path:
		export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/development/flutter/bin"

content.title: Run Flutter Doctor
bullets: You’ll see warnings (e.g., Android Studio not installed). Fix them next.

content.title: Install Android Studio (for Android Development)
bullets:
Launch Android Studio → Install Flutter and Dart plugins:
		Go to Preferences → Plugins → Search for "Flutter" → Install.

Configure Android SDK:

Open Android Studio → More Actions → SDK Manager.

Install the latest Android SDK and Android SDK Command-line Tools.

content.title: Set Up iOS Simulator
bullets:
Open Xcode → Preferences → Locations.
Ensure Command Line Tools is set to the latest Xcode version.

content.title: Install Visual Studio Code (Optional but Recommended)
bullets: Open VS Code → Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X) → Search for "Flutter" → Install it.
This will also prompt you to install Dart (click Yes).

content.title: Create Your First Flutter App
bullets: Open VS Code or Android Studio.

Create a new Flutter project:
		`flutter create my_first_app`

Navigate to the project folder:
		`cd my_first_app`
You should see a demo app running on your emulator.
